title: Social protection expands globally while climate-vulnerable populations remain least protected and just-transition capacity stays uneven
source_unit: International Labour Organization, World Social Protection Report 2024-26: Universal social protection for climate action and a just transition
geography: Global and regional social-protection coverage, expenditure, climate vulnerability, life-course benefits, and just-transition policy indicators

denominator.unit: global population assessed for effective coverage by at least one social-protection benefit

covered_2023.unit: percent of the global population covered by at least one social-protection benefit

covered_2015.unit: percent of the global population covered in 2015

unprotected.unit: billion people with no social-protection coverage

observations.method: ILO compilation of national administrative data, surveys, modeled estimates, and the World Social Protection Database for SDG indicator 1.3.1.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage estimates use different national systems, definitions, data years, and methodological enhancements; having a benefit does not establish adequacy, take-up, continuity, or protection from a specific shock.
observations.subgroup: People outside formal systems, low-income populations, informal workers, children, older people, people with disabilities, migrants, and households exposed to climate shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase since 2015 is substantial institutional progress even though effective coverage remains incomplete and uneven across countries and population groups.

denominator.unit: countries identified as most vulnerable to the climate crisis

unprotected_most_vulnerable.unit: percent of people without any social-protection coverage in the 20 most climate-vulnerable countries

unprotected_count.unit: million people without coverage in those 20 countries

unprotected_50_countries.unit: percent of people without coverage across the 50 most climate-vulnerable countries

observations.method: ILO comparison of effective social-protection coverage with climate-vulnerability classifications and country population estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The relationship is a cross-country distributional pattern, not a causal estimate; vulnerability rankings, coverage years, and country conditions can change.
observations.subgroup: People in climate-vulnerable countries, climate-exposed workers and households, rural and informal populations, and communities with limited fiscal capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some countries can improve preparedness through targeted, shock-responsive, or regionally supported systems even when baseline coverage is low.

denominator.unit: global population and children assessed for effective social-protection coverage

children_uncovered.unit: percent of children without effective social-protection coverage

women_covered.unit: percent of women with effective social-protection coverage

men_covered.unit: percent of men with effective social-protection coverage

child_benefit_coverage.unit: percent of children aged 0-18 covered by child cash benefits

observations.method: ILO life-course compilation of effective coverage by sex, age, and benefit type from national and modeled social-protection data.
observations.uncertainty: Sex, age, and benefit measures are not interchangeable and may reflect legal eligibility, effective access, and differing country data quality; coverage does not measure benefit adequacy or safety.
observations.subgroup: Children, women, caregivers, people with disabilities, and households relying on child, family, maternity, health, or income-security benefits.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate coverage can conceal meaningful gains in particular programs or countries, and social protection is only one component of care, health, and income security.

denominator.unit: countries reporting average public expenditure as a share of GDP

social_protection_excluding_health.unit: percent of GDP allocated on average to social protection excluding healthcare

healthcare.unit: percent of GDP allocated on average to healthcare

combined.unit: percent of GDP for social protection and healthcare combined

policy_role.value: social protection can cushion mitigation costs, support adaptation, and enable transitions into greener work when paired with labour-market and climate policy

observations.method: ILO compilation of public social-protection and healthcare expenditure with report-level analysis of climate adaptation, mitigation, and just-transition functions.
observations.uncertainty: Global averages hide large income-group and country differences; expenditure levels do not establish delivery quality, distribution, or the effectiveness of a particular climate policy.
observations.subgroup: Low-income countries, workers and enterprises facing transition costs, households exposed to climate shocks, and public agencies financing social-protection floors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher expenditure is not automatically more protective; targeting, adequacy, fiscal sustainability, institutional capacity, and worker voice also shape outcomes.

related_sources.claim: ILO figures page provides the report's headline coverage and expenditure indicators.
ILO social-protection topic page provides complementary financing and policy context.

boundary: This record adds a global public-system route linking social-protection coverage, climate vulnerability, life-course and gender gaps, fiscal capacity, and just-transition policy. It uses publication-level aggregate indicators, not respondent-level histories, individual benefit records, household panels, or causal estimates of climate or welfare-policy effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official ILO publication page and accompanying figures page were reviewed for coverage, climate vulnerability, life-course and gender gaps, expenditure, and just-transition claims.
